title: Cybersecurity Analyst Salary 2026: US Pay by Experience Level
metaDescription: Cybersecurity analyst salary 2026: BLS median $129,180, entry pay near $90,000, senior pay near $180,000, top earners above $227,000, and 21% growth.
headline: Cybersecurity Analyst Salary 2026: Complete US Pay Guide

sections.title: What Cybersecurity Analysts Earn in 2026
sections.content:
The US Bureau of Labor Statistics puts the median wage for information security analysts at $129,180 per year, based on May 2025 data, with the lowest tenth earning under $75,090 and the highest tenth earning over $199,850. Job postings aggregators report lower averages, around $100,000, because they mix junior and senior roles differently.

Levels.fyi data from large technology and finance employers shows median total compensation near $125,000, with the top tenth reaching about $240,000. The spread shows why comparing like with like matters: base salary, bonuses and stock can differ sharply between employers.

sections.title: Pay by Experience and Certification
sections.content:
Entry-level analysts typically start near $73,500 to $90,000, mid-career analysts earn around $124,000 and senior analysts reach roughly $180,000. Experience, security clearance, cloud skills and certifications such as Security+, CISSP and cloud security credentials all push pay upward.

Industry matters too: finance, defence and large technology firms usually pay above the national median, while smaller firms and non-profits pay less but may offer remote work or broader responsibilities. Location still moves pay by roughly 15 to 30 percent between metro areas.

sections.title: Outlook and How to Raise Your Pay
sections.content:
Employment for information security analysts is projected to grow 21 percent from 2025 to 2035, with about 14,100 openings a year, making it one of the fastest-growing technology roles. Demand is driven by ransomware, cloud migration and stricter compliance rules.

To raise pay fastest, analysts should specialise in detection engineering, cloud security or incident response, build a portfolio of real investigations and earn respected certifications. Changing employers after two to three years of strong results remains the most reliable way to jump a pay band.

faqs.q: What is the average cybersecurity analyst salary in the US in 2026?
faqs.a: The official median is $129,180 per year according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, while job-posting averages sit near $100,000 and large-employer total compensation medians sit near $125,000. The right benchmark depends on your employer type, because federal data covers all employers while Levels.fyi skews toward large technology and finance firms.

faqs.q: How much do entry-level cybersecurity analysts earn?
faqs.a: Entry-level cybersecurity analysts typically earn between $73,500 and $90,000 in base pay, depending on location, employer size and certifications. Candidates with internships, a Security+ certification or hands-on lab experience usually start at the upper end of that range, while fully remote junior roles can pay less.

faqs.q: Which cybersecurity certifications raise salary the most?
faqs.a: Security+ is the standard entry credential, while CISSP, cloud security certifications and GIAC credentials are linked to the biggest pay jumps at mid-career and senior levels. Employers also reward practical skills in detection, cloud platforms and incident response, so a certification paired with real project experience beats a certificate alone.

faqs.q: Is cybersecurity analyst a good career for salary growth?
faqs.a: Yes, with 21 percent projected employment growth to 2035 and about 14,100 annual openings, cybersecurity analysts enjoy strong demand and fast pay progression. Analysts who specialise, earn respected certifications and move into senior or engineering roles can roughly double entry-level pay within five to eight years.
